data.title: Spring
data.tagline: Create motion that settles with weight and elasticity
data.description: Spring motion is defined by physical-style values such as stiffness and damping rather than only a fixed curve. It suits direct manipulation and elements that need to settle into place. Too much bounce makes routine actions feel slow and unstable.

use: A playful control with direct manipulation
avoid: Use a spring where precise timing must match another event

lessonPractice.title: A dragged card should return to its target after release without continuing to wobble. What is the better approach?

options.label: Use the existing animation system for one small overshoot that settles quickly, and move directly to the target under reduced motion
options.feedback: Correct. A spring fits settling after direct manipulation, but the bounce must serve the position change and have a stable reduced alternative.

options.label: Keep the card bouncing until the user clicks again so its elasticity remains obvious
options.feedback: Continuous bouncing prevents the state from settling and distracts from the next task.

options.label: Apply the same strong spring to every button, dialog, and list item for complete consistency
options.feedback: Objects differ in distance, meaning, and risk; forcing all of them to bounce weakens hierarchy and disrupts serious actions.

data.agentPrompt: Use the animation approach already present in the project to add a subtle spring when a draggable card returns to its target after release. Animate only its position; do not change the card content or drag rules. Allow at most one small overshoot and make it settle quickly. When reduced motion is enabled, return directly to the target. Test short drags, long drags, repeated drags, and reduced-motion mode, and confirm the card neither keeps wobbling nor covers nearby content.
